preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 2 * 10**5 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and 1 <= int(line) <= 2 * 10**5])
preconditions.description: Each test case has n cities where n is between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(c) == n and all(1 <= ci <= 10**6 for ci in c) for c in [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit() and len(line.split()) == n])
preconditions.description: Each test case has n initial flag colors c_i, where each c_i is between 1 and 1,000,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(d) == n and all(1 <= di <= 10**6 for di in d) for d in [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit() and len(line.split()) == n])
preconditions.description: Each test case has n desired flag colors d_i, where each d_i is between 1 and 1,000,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(roads) == n - 1 for roads in [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit() and len(line.split()) == 2])
preconditions.description: Each test case has exactly n-1 roads, forming a tree (connected and acyclic).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n and x != y for x, y in roads)
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct cities within the range 1 to n.

postconditions.description: The first line of output for each test case is either 'Yes' or 'No', indicating whether a valid route exists.

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip() == 'Yes') == (all(c_i != d_i for c_i, d_i in zip(c, d)) or any(k > 0 and all(c_i ^ d_i == 1 for c_i, d_i in zip(c, d)) for k, route in valid_routes))
postconditions.description: If 'Yes', there exists a route such that after traversing it, the flag colors match the desired colors d_i. If 'No', no such route exists.

postconditions.expression: all(len(route) == k for k, route in valid_routes if k > 0)
postconditions.description: If 'Yes', the route length k is exactly the number of cities in the route.

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= u <= n for u in route) for k, route in valid_routes if k > 0)
postconditions.description: Each city in the route is within the valid range 1 to n.

postconditions.expression: all(all(route[i] != route[i+1] or i == len(route) - 1 for i in range(len(route) - 1)) for k, route in valid_routes if k > 0)
postconditions.description: The route is a valid path in the tree, meaning consecutive cities are connected by a road.

postconditions.expression: all(k == 0 or (k == min(len(route) for k, route in valid_routes)) for k, route in valid_routes if k > 0)
postconditions.description: If 'Yes', the route length k is the shortest possible among all valid routes.
